response.overview: INTERSTICE explores time as a layered and nonlinear element. A found film test—a seemingly fixed moment—is manipulated through scratching, re-photographing, looping, and additional animation to disrupt and reshape its temporal continuity. The direct animation, if projected traditionally, would transpire subliminally. But by creating loops within loops, new interactions between frames are revealed. The figure becomes a spectral presence, caught between motion and stillness—like a fleeting thought or memory folding back on itself. Time becomes elastic, with moments repeating, shifting, and evolving rather than progressing forward. The result is a meditation on motion, memory, and the fluidity of perception.
response.title: INTERSTICE
